A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
isolated pediatric distal radius fractures can be treated by simple splinting and early orthopaedic follow up with no reduction and no residual deformity.

isolated distal radius fractures in skeletally immature children that have 15° or less of angulation and are less than 1-cm short will heal and remodel completely without any significant residual clinical or functional sequel.

pediatric distal radius fractures that are angulated or shortened less than 15 degrees and 1 centimeter, respectively, can be splinted in the emergency room without reduction.
